blocks.p: They walked him the last of the way.

The hall was long and white, and it opened into another, and that into another. The stone was cool underfoot, and the air was still. He went slowly, because he was old and the slippers they had given him were thin, and between his wrists a fine white chain rang a little at every step, the way a spoon rings against a cup.

He was very old. His hair had gone white and then nearly gone, and his hands were spotted and would not keep still. Across the base of the left thumb ran a thin shining scar, a burn let heal on its own. It was the oldest thing about him.
A small man walked beside him with a hand on his arm, lightly, as if the arm might break. He had a mild young face, and there was a little earth under his fingernails, and he was smiling.
Far behind, where the stone changed, a woman in a grey coat stood between two figures in white and watched him go.
The old man had come this way before, many times, in another life, when halls went quiet as he came into them and he had liked it more than he should have.
Ahead of them stood the doors, tall and plain and shut.
“Don’t be afraid,” the small man said, very kindly.
And before the old man had reached them, the doors began to open on their own, as they always had for him, with one long low sound, and a long cool breath came out to meet him.
